clue.text: It's a dance, anyhow, and no fag

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old fashion, so the letters of the words after it are jumbled

parts.note: the eight letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will dance regardless, and without a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' looks like a casual aside but signals rearranging AND NO FAG; 'It's' simply introduces the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time, often played with castanets.

clue.text: Paradoxically, these men come to the fore in the past

definitions.text: Paradoxically, these men come to the fore in the past

parts.words: Paradoxically, these men come to the fore in the past
parts.note: come to the fore means become prominent, but here these men are prefixed by fore to name ancestors

explanation.surface: Men of old who were once prominent.
explanation.walkthrough: Put 'fore' in front of the word and you get ancestors, people of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Male parents; with fore- in front they become ancestors.

clue.text: Pearl's mother

parts.note: a person named Pearl's mum, but really the substance called mother-of-pearl

explanation.surface: A woman called Pearl's mum.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearl looks like a girl's name; 'mother of pearl' is the iridescent shell lining.
explanation.definitionFit: The iridescent shell lining is called mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Singer returns to the heart of Scotland

indicators.note: returns means the extracted letters are turned to run in the reverse direction
the heart of a word is its central letters, here the middle four of Scotland

explanation.surface: A vocalist comes back home to central Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle four letters of Scotland, OTLA, are reversed by 'returns'.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice part, the lowest female or highest male, and a vocalist in that range.

clue.text: It may give a measure of light and heat

definitions.text: It may give a measure of light and heat

parts.words: It may give a measure of light and heat
parts.note: an instrument recording how much fuel is used for lamps and fires

explanation.surface: Something that measures illumination and warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas once supplied both lighting and heating, so its meter measured both.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that records household fuel consumption.

clue.text: It takes the floor as favourite at the Motor Show

parts.note: a car is what is displayed at a motor show
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A vehicle tipped as the star exhibit at the motor show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the floor' suggests a dancer or speaker; here it means covers the floor. The pet is placed 'at' the car, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug or fitted covering lies over the floor of a room.

clue.text: Rotund, well-built Londoner ?

parts.note: seemingly a portly, sturdy man from London, but really a round, solidly built London concert hall

explanation.surface: A stout, sturdy Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Londoner' is a building: the round Victorian concert hall in Kensington.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed circular concert venue in Kensington, London.

clue.text: He is, in part, distinguished

parts.note: in part looks like partly, but means in a stage role, someone who shines when playing a role

explanation.surface: A man who is partly eminent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' means in a theatrical role, not partially.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on stage, an actor.

clue.text: Just the night for play

parts.note: a good evening for fun, but really the night that names a Shakespeare comedy

explanation.surface: An evening ideal for having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is Shakespeare's comedy named after the last night of Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal that precedes Night in the title of a Shakespeare comedy.

clue.text: Bearing of a novel beau

definitions.meaning: deportment, a manner of carrying oneself; an old word for conduct
Beau ___ is the title of P C Wren's novel about the Foreign Legion

explanation.surface: The demeanour of a fresh boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new' but means a book: Beau Geste.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means conduct or deed, and is the surname of the hero of a Foreign Legion novel.

clue.text: The historian with nothing to say to us

parts.note: tacit means silent, unspoken
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historian who keeps silent when addressing us.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman historian's name splits into a word for silent plus US; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman writer of the Annals and Histories, chronicling the early Empire.

clue.text: Give me back a couple to hold

indicators.note: back here means the word me is turned round to read in the other direction

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a couple of game birds

explanation.surface: A request to return something and keep a pair of items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM; 'Give' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone in your arms is to hug them tightly.

clue.text: Smooth part of some ventures

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something smooths out a portion of various business undertakings.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'somE VENtures'.
explanation.definitionFit: A level, flat surface has no bumps, so smooth and level are synonyms.

clue.text: One's marriage portion ?

parts.note: a marriage portion is a dowry, but read literally it is the share of a marriage that is one's spouse

explanation.surface: A question about the dowry someone brings to a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marriage portion' means a dowry in old usage; the clue reads it as the other half of a married couple.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular name for one's wife or husband.

clue.text: Its appearance suggests there's something brewing

definitions.text: Its appearance suggests there's something brewing

parts.words: Its appearance suggests there's something brewing
parts.note: something brewing usually means trouble ahead, but here it is a pot of tea being made

explanation.surface: An ominous sign of impending trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something brewing' suggests trouble; it is tea brewing in the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cups, saucers and pot for serving the drink.

clue.text: No one can accuse him of not being painstaking

definitions.text: No one can accuse him of not being painstaking

parts.words: No one can accuse him of not being painstaking
parts.note: painstaking usually means careful, but split as pains-taking it describes a person who takes, or endures, pain

explanation.surface: A tribute to a diligent worker whom nobody could call careless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'painstaking' as 'taking pains': someone who puts up with pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who endures pain or illness is a patient, one afflicted.

clue.text: A hand to warm a theatre manager's heart

definitions.meaning: in poker, three of a kind with a pair

definitions.text: to warm a theatre manager's heart
definitions.meaning: a sell-out audience with every seat taken

explanation.surface: Applause that pleases a theatre manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A hand' suggests applause but is a poker hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker combination of three and two of a kind, and an auditorium with every seat sold.

clue.text: Outcome of shell-bursts

parts.note: shell-bursts suggest artillery, but here eggshells break open and chicks come out

explanation.surface: The result of an artillery barrage.
explanation.walkthrough: The military picture is a decoy: the shells are eggshells.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicks emerging from eggs is the brood that results when eggs break open.

clue.text: No chance for a dance

indicators.note: for here means the letters of no chance stand in for a jumbled form, the setter's signal to rearrange them

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A dancer is told there is no hope.
explanation.walkthrough: An older style of clue with a slight anagram signal: NO CHANCE rearranged gives the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately Baroque dance on a repeated bass line.

clue.text: But in Irish mouths they're ludicrously off target

definitions.text: But in Irish mouths they're ludicrously off target

parts.words: But in Irish mouths they're ludicrously off target
parts.note: on a dartboard or rifle range these are hits in the very centre; an Irish one is a ludicrous self-contradictory statement

explanation.surface: Irish speakers miss the mark in a comical way.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'Irish bull' is an old term for a laughably self-contradictory statement, the opposite of a hit in the centre of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd, illogical remarks were traditionally called Irish ones, while centre hits on a target share the name.

clue.text: What this young beast's mother did

definitions.text: What this young beast's mother did

parts.words: What this young beast's mother did
parts.note: the mother gave birth to her young, and the past tense of the verb to bear names her species

explanation.surface: A question about what a young animal's mother did.
explanation.walkthrough: The mother 'bore cub'; read as 'bear cub' it names the young animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A young ursine animal.

clue.text: Strains we hear, inducing love ?

indicators.note: we hear says the word for strains is to be taken by its sound, spelt differently

parts.note: to strain a liquid is to pass it through filters, so strains means filters

explanation.surface: Musical strains heard as a romantic, love-inducing melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strains' looks like music but is the verb meaning filters; 'we hear' gives a word sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Love potions are drinks believed to make the drinker fall in love.

clue.text: Not that its operations usually take place here

definitions.text: Not that its operations usually take place here

parts.words: Not that its operations usually take place here
parts.note: a doctor's consulting room is named for operations, though most visits there involve none

explanation.surface: Operations rarely happen at this place after all.
explanation.walkthrough: A British GP's consulting rooms are called this, though little cutting is done there.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's practice premises bear the name, as does the medical branch of cutting.

clue.text: She comes up with something of value

indicators.note: in a down clue, comes up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an asset is something of value

explanation.surface: A woman arrives bearing something precious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' reverses ASSET in this down clue to give a girl's name; 'She' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it fits 'she' as a female person.

clue.text: Odium can bore her, terribly

indicators.note: terribly here means badly, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Hatred can be really tedious to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' looks like an intensifier for 'bore' but signals the anagram of CAN BORE HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean intense hatred or loathing.

clue.text: Box in wooden fashion

parts.note: box as fighting with fists, done for practice and not in earnest; a mast or pole of timber shares the name

explanation.surface: Fighting stiffly, like a wooden boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: To spar is to box in practice; a spar is also a wooden pole, hence 'wooden'.
explanation.definitionFit: Practice boxing is the verb sense, and a ship's wooden pole the noun sense.

clue.text: The yard is constantly in occupation

indicators.note: constantly in says the answer stays held within the letters of the final word of the clue, the way a resident occupies a place

explanation.surface: A courtyard that is always being used.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a busy yard; 'constantly in' points to the run of letters held within 'occupation', and 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved courtyard or terrace beside a house is a kind of yard.

clue.text: The mad race to get land

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

parts.note: the four letters of this word are the fodder

explanation.surface: A frantic race to grab territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' signals rearranging RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of area for fields, so it stands for a plot of ground.

clue.text: Relations who put us in the money

indicators.note: in says the word us is put inside the word for money

parts.note: coins are money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Family members who make us rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put us in the money' reads as making us wealthy, a picture of rich relatives; the phrase is really an instruction for placing one word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Children of one's aunts or uncles are family members, kin.

clue.text: It provides no knotty problem for the nudist

definitions.text: It provides no knotty problem for the nudist

parts.words: It provides no knotty problem for the nudist
parts.note: a knotty problem is a tricky one, but here it is literally an item that must be tied in a knot, which a naked person need not wear

explanation.surface: A naked person has no awkward dilemmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knotty' means difficult in the surface but literally something knotted at the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth knotted round the collar of a shirt.

clue.text: His products were transported by the back-yard

definitions.text: His products were transported by the back-yard

parts.words: His products were transported by the back-yard
parts.note: the products are beers and ales, delivered to the back yard of a pub, and a yard is also a tall glass of ale

explanation.surface: Goods carried in through the rear yard.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'yard of ale' is a tall glass of beer; the products are beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of beer, whose barrels go in at the back of the pub.

clue.text: " What have kings that privates have not too, Save ——" (Hen. V)

definitions.text: What have kings that privates have not too, Save ——" (Hen. V)

parts.words: What have kings that privates have not too, Save ——" (Hen. V)
parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Henry V, where the king asks what kings have that commoners lack and answers with a word for pomp and ritual

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's Henry V with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in King Henry's speech on the eve of Agincourt: 'Save ceremony, save general ceremony?'
explanation.definitionFit: Formal ritual and pomp is the only thing the king says monarchs have over commoners.
